note: New path only (kit install/plan/verify/update). The legacy installer keeps reading mcp/manifest.json and mcp/allowlist.json. Fields: 04_DESIGN 3.6, rules: kit/mcp_catalog.py.

sequential-thinking.license: package says 'SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE' (modelcontextprotocol/servers, moving from MIT to Apache-2.0); 2025.12.18 declared MIT
sequential-thinking.network_egress: npm registry download on first start; the server itself is not expected to use the network (not verified)
sequential-thinking.lifecycle_scripts: registry package has no install scripts ('prepare' runs only for git installs)

playwright.disabled_reason: opens a real browser and visits any URL the agent chooses; first start downloads the package and may need browser binaries. Opt in with --mcp playwright
playwright.network_egress: npm registry download on first start; the browser reaches any site the agent opens
playwright.file_access: browser profile and downloads in a temporary directory; reads files the agent uploads
playwright.lifecycle_scripts: none in @playwright/mcp@0.0.84, playwright and playwright-core 1.65.0-alpha-2026-10-30 (npm view, 2026-11-06)

context7.disabled_reason: sends the library names and questions the agent looks up to context7.com. Opt in with --mcp context7; works without a key (lower rate limits)
context7.network_egress: npm registry download on first start; context7.com API for every lookup
context7.lifecycle_scripts: none in @upstash/context7-mcp@4.5.1 or its 12 direct dependencies (npm view, 2026-11-06)

credentials.purpose: higher rate limits and private repositories; without it the server runs keyless (an unset ${CONTEXT7_API_KEY} placeholder is ignored by 4.5.1)

fetch.disabled_reason: fetches arbitrary URLs: can send task data outside the workspace. Listed only (no pinned version)

git.disabled_reason: exposes git operations including remote sync; the agents already run git through the shell with approval. Listed only (no pinned version)

filesystem.disabled_reason: duplicates the agents' own file access and widens the reachable paths. Listed only (no pinned version)

codebase-memory.disabled_reason: indexes the whole repository; on first start it downloads a native binary from the project's GitHub Releases and keeps a background daemon and cache under ~/.cache/codebase-memory-mcp. Never run its `install` subcommand (it edits agent configs). Opt in with --mcp codebase-memory
codebase-memory.network_egress: PyPI download on first start, then the native binary from github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp releases; the index itself stays local (not verified at runtime)
codebase-memory.file_access: reads every file in the workspace; writes its index and daemon state under ~/.cache/codebase-memory-mcp
codebase-memory.lifecycle_scripts: uvx (PyPI) on purpose: the npm package of the same name has a postinstall script (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-13, 2026-11-08)

markitdown.disabled_reason: alpha release; its convert tool reads any file the agent names and fetches any http(s) URL, so task data can leave the workspace. Opt in with --mcp markitdown
markitdown.network_egress: PyPI download on first start; any URL the agent asks it to convert
markitdown.file_access: any local file the agent names (file: URIs), not only the workspace
markitdown.lifecycle_scripts: Python wheel, no install hooks run by uvx

inspo.disabled_reason: first start downloads a ~14 MB design catalogue from Vercel Blob storage; semantic search sends your queries to Together AI when TOGETHER_API_KEY is set. Never run its `install` subcommand (it writes agent configs). Opt in with --mcp inspo
inspo.network_egress: npm registry download on first start; the catalogue from Vercel Blob storage; Together AI embeddings for semantic search (only with a key); get_design_system(live) fetches the public page it is asked about
inspo.file_access: none expected outside its npm cache
inspo.lifecycle_scripts: not checked for 0.2.0 dependencies (UNVERIFIED); the kit runs nothing

credentials.purpose: Together AI embeddings behind semantic search and find_similar (README at the pinned commit); optional per the 2026-11-08 review, not checked at runtime. The README names no page for creating the key, so where to get it is UNVERIFIED: see the README

rea.disabled_reason: agent runtime with 42 npm dependencies; its `rea-agents setup` command installs into your home folder and must never be run for this entry (the project-scope stdio server is `rea-agents mcp`). Opt in with --mcp rea
rea.network_egress: npm registry download on first start; whatever model providers and tools you configure in rea (not verified at runtime)
rea.file_access: the workspace the agent points it at
rea.lifecycle_scripts: a `prepare` script, which npm runs only for git installs, not for the registry package

scrapling.disabled_reason: web scraping (sends requests to any site); its MCP server needs the Python package (v0.5.1) and `scrapling install` to download browsers before it can start, which the kit does not do. Listed only (no runnable command)
scrapling.network_egress: any URL; browser downloads during `scrapling install`
